claims.text: A W-Ti-Zr-Hf refractory high-entropy alloy can be used as an interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
The W-Ti-Zr-Hf interlayer has enhanced compatibility with W and CuCrZr.
The W-Ti-Zr-Hf interlayer is resistant to extreme fusion-reactor conditions.
The proposed interlayer is 100 μm thick and has the composition W50Ti20Zr15Hf15 in atomic percent.
The proposed joint is intended to operate at temperatures up to 1000°C under high-energy particle irradiation.
A stable nanoscale oxide layer forms at the W-Ti-Zr-Hf/CuCrZr interface.
The nanoscale interfacial oxide layer enhances thermal stability.
The nanoscale interfacial oxide layer enhances mechanical stability.
The high-entropy alloy composition promotes sluggish diffusion.
The high-entropy alloy composition reduces the formation of deleterious phases.
Sluggish diffusion and reduced formation of deleterious phases improve interlayer compatibility and resistance to extreme environments.
The interlayer produces a 30% increase in thermal-shock resistance relative to a W/CuCrZr joint without an interlayer.
A W/CuCrZr joint without an interlayer fails after 50 thermal cycles.
A 30% improvement over the stated 50-cycle baseline corresponds to 65 thermal cycles to failure.
The interlayer may lose performance above 1200°C.
The interlayer may lose performance at high irradiation doses.

contradictions.description: A 30% increase over the 50-cycle baseline predicts 65 cycles. Twenty percent below 65 is 52 cycles, not 40 cycles. The stated fewer-than-40 threshold is approximately 38.5% below the predicted outcome and therefore conflicts with the accompanying claim that it is 20% below the prediction.
